Identity (naming and use only, never placement): PROSEA (Plant Resources of South-East Asia) Cyamopsis tetragonoloba, https://prosea.prota4u.org/view.aspx?id=3002, vernacular names "Guar, cluster bean, Siam bean (En)"; "sweet and tender young pods are consumed as a vegetable in north-western and southern India". The row is the fresh pod as a vegetable; "guar" alone is not aliased (guar gum and guar meal name processed products). Dried seed and guar gum forms follow their own rules (abstain).

Identity (naming only, never placement): Purdue University NewCROP fact sheet, https://hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/CropFactSheets/bael.html, common names "English: Wood apple, Bengal Quince; Hindi: Bael, Sirphal" (Aegle marmelos); the fact sheet describes the fresh half-ripe fruit as eaten and gives cultivar pulp and flavour notes. "Wood apple" is not aliased because it also names another fruit (Limonia). Dried, pulp, juice, candy and powder forms follow the fruit rules (abstain or their own markers).
